concepts.title: Geographical Expanse and Territorial Extent of India
concepts.definition: The total spatial expanse of India covering its geographical surface area along with north-to-south and east-to-west linear dimensions.
concepts.key_idea: India covers about 3.28 million square kilometers with distinct latitudinal and longitudinal boundaries.
question_patterns: what is the total geographical area of India
calculate the approximate distance from Ladakh to Kanyakumari
find the east to west distance from Arunachal Pradesh to Kuchchh
how much area does the landmass of India occupy
state the linear extent of India from north to south

solution_steps.explain: India covers approximately 3.28 million square kilometers of total land area.
The north-south extent from Ladakh to Kanyakumari measures about 3,200 km.
The east-west extent from Arunachal Pradesh to Kuchchh measures about 2,900 km.

concepts.title: Longitudinal Time Difference Calculation
concepts.definition: Computation of local time variation between two longitudes based on the constant rate of four minutes per degree of longitudinal separation.
concepts.key_idea: Earth rotation causes a local time change of four minutes for each degree of longitude.
question_patterns: calculate local time difference for longitudinal difference of {degree_diff} degrees
find time gap in hours between two longitudes separated by {degree_diff} degrees
how much time difference occurs over a longitude extent of {degree_diff} degrees
determine local time variation across {degree_diff} degrees longitude
what is the time offset in hours for {degree_diff} degrees longitudinal difference

solution_steps.action: calculate total time difference in minutes
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the longitudinal difference in degrees by 4 minutes per degree.
Divide the total minutes by 60 to obtain time difference in hours.

concepts.title: Locational Setting and Latitudinal-Longitudinal Boundaries
concepts.definition: The precise global coordinates defining the mainland of India in the northern and eastern hemispheres, including key latitude lines.
concepts.key_idea: India lies in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres, bisected by the Tropic of Cancer at 23 degrees 30 minutes N.
question_patterns: what are the latitudinal limits of mainland India
find the longitudinal extent of India
which latitude line divides India into roughly two equal halves
identify the hemisphere in which India is situated
state the coordinate extent of the Indian mainland

solution_steps.explain: Mainland India extends between 8 degrees 4 minutes N and 37 degrees 6 minutes N latitudes.
India extends between 68 degrees 7 minutes E and 97 degrees 25 minutes E longitudes.
The Tropic of Cancer (23 degrees 30 minutes N) passes almost halfway through the country.

concepts.title: India's Land Neighbours and Marine Boundaries
concepts.definition: The geographical relationships of India with adjacent countries sharing land borders or maritime boundaries across surrounding seas.
concepts.key_idea: Seven countries border India by land while island neighbours lie across water channels such as the Palk Strait.
question_patterns: name the countries sharing land boundaries with India
which water feature separates Sri Lanka from India
identify the island neighbours of India located to the south
how many countries share land borders with India
find which neighbouring nations do not have access to an ocean

solution_steps.explain: Seven countries share terrestrial borders with India: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar.
Sri Lanka and Maldives are southern island neighbours; Sri Lanka is separated from India by the Palk Strait.

concepts.title: Political and Administrative Structure of India
concepts.definition: The governance framework dividing India into states created primarily on a linguistic basis and centrally governed union territories.
concepts.key_idea: India comprises 28 states and 8 union territories with New Delhi as the national capital.
question_patterns: how many states and union territories exist in India
what is the capital city of India
on what major basis were states formed in India
find which states share a common capital
describe administrative divisions of India

solution_steps.explain: India is divided into 28 states and 8 Union Territories.

solution_steps.action: identify national capital and state formation basis
solution_steps.explain: Delhi is the national capital, and states were formed predominantly based on regional languages.

concepts.title: Himalayan Mountain Range Structure
concepts.definition: The northernmost mountain barrier of India, divided into three parallel structural longitudinal zones.
concepts.key_idea: The Himalayas consist of Himadri (Great Himalayas), Himachal (Middle Himalayas), and Shiwalik (Outer Himalayas).
question_patterns: name the three parallel ranges of the Himalayas
which is the northernmost range of the Himalayas containing world famous peaks
identify the southernmost range of the Himalayan mountain system
where are popular hill stations situated in the Himalayas
what does the word Himalaya mean

solution_steps.explain: Great Himalaya or Himadri is the northernmost range and contains the highest peaks.
Middle Himalaya or Himachal lies south of Himadri and houses popular hill stations.
Shiwalik is the southernmost Himalayan range.

concepts.title: Northern Indian Plains and Alluvial River Systems
concepts.definition: Flat and fertile plains located south of the Himalayas formed by silt deposits carried by major river networks.
concepts.key_idea: Fine alluvial soil brought by the Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra and tributaries creates highly fertile, densely populated plains.
question_patterns: how are the Northern Indian plains formed
why do a large number of people reside in the Northern plains
name the major river systems contributing to alluvial deposits in the northern plains
what is an alluvial deposit
define a river tributary in geographical terms

solution_steps.explain: Rivers like Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra deposit fine alluvial soil during flooding, creating flat plains.
Fertile agricultural land and level terrain make these plains highly suitable for cultivation and settlement.

concepts.title: Peninsular Plateau and Relief Features
concepts.definition: A triangular elevated landform with uneven terrain south of the northern plains, rich in mineral resources and framed by hill ranges.
concepts.key_idea: The plateau is bounded by Aravali, Vindhya, Satpura ranges and drained westward by Narmada and Tapi rivers into the Arabian Sea.
question_patterns: describe the shape and relief of the Peninsular plateau
which two major rivers flow westwards into the Arabian Sea
what is the oldest mountain range in India
identify mountain ranges bordering the Peninsular plateau
which minerals are abundantly found in the Peninsular plateau

solution_steps.explain: The Peninsular plateau is triangular with uneven relief, containing numerous hill ranges and valleys.
Narmada and Tapi flow west between Vindhya and Satpura ranges into the Arabian Sea.

solution_steps.action: identify bounding hill ranges and minerals
solution_steps.explain: Bordered by Aravali, Western Ghats (Sahyadris), and Eastern Ghats; rich in coal and iron ore.

concepts.title: Coastal Plains, Deltas, and Island Archipelagos
concepts.definition: Coastal regions bordering the peninsular plateau along with offshore island groups formed by coral polyps or sub-sea topography.
concepts.key_idea: Narrow western and broad eastern coastal plains, Sundarbans delta, coral Lakshadweep in Arabian Sea, and Andaman & Nicobar in Bay of Bengal.
question_patterns: compare the western and eastern coastal plains of India
which major delta is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers
why is Lakshadweep classified as a coral island group
name the Indian islands situated in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
which rivers drain eastwards into the Bay of Bengal forming fertile deltas

solution_steps.explain: Western coastal plains are narrow; eastern coastal plains are broader with east-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri).
Ganga and Brahmaputra form the triangular Sundarbans delta at their mouth in the Bay of Bengal.
Lakshadweep in Arabian Sea is made of coral polyp skeletons; Andaman and Nicobar lie in the Bay of Bengal.
